course.learn: Isolation separates a risky or sensitive system from other resources so compromise cannot easily spread. Physical isolation and air gaps provide stronger separation than ordinary logical controls.
course.why: Reducing connectivity reduces attack paths and lateral movement.
course.example: A malware-analysis workstation is placed on an isolated network with no route to production systems.
course.exam: Air-gapped means no normal network connection. Quarantine is often temporary isolation during an incident.

defs: Dividing a network into controlled zones to limit access and lateral movement.

course.learn: Network segmentation separates systems into different trust zones so traffic must cross controlled boundaries. VLANs, subnets, ACLs, and firewalls are common mechanisms.
course.why: Segmentation limits lateral movement and reduces the blast radius of a compromised host.
course.example: Guest Wi-Fi is placed in a separate VLAN with firewall rules that block access to internal servers.
course.exam: If the goal is containment or preventing one network from freely reaching another, segmentation is a strong answer.

course.learn: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) separates centralized control logic from the devices that forward traffic. Controllers program network behavior dynamically through software.
course.why: Centralized programmability can improve automation and segmentation but makes the controller and management APIs high-value security targets.
course.example: A controller automatically pushes segmentation rules to switches when a new workload is deployed.
course.exam: Control plane is centralized/software-driven; protect controller access, APIs, backups, and policy integrity.

course.learn: On-premises infrastructure is owned or operated within an organization's facilities rather than consumed as a public cloud service. The organization has more direct control but also carries more responsibility for physical systems, maintenance, and capacity.
course.why: Architecture decisions trade control, cost, scalability, staffing, and recovery requirements.
course.example: A company runs its own server room, network equipment, virtualization cluster, and storage rather than hosting those workloads in a public cloud.
course.exam: On-prem usually means greater direct responsibility; cloud shifts some infrastructure responsibility to the provider.

breakdown.term: Is the deployment of IT infrastructure within an organization's physical location
breakdown.explanation: Infrastructure monitoring observes networks, cloud configuration, appliances, links, and supporting resources. NSM analyzes network behavior, while CSPM evaluates cloud security posture and misconfiguration.

breakdown.term: Can tailor the systems to specific needs
breakdown.explanation: System monitoring focuses on endpoints and hosts. Endpoint Protection Platforms (EPP) detect or prevent malicious endpoint activity, while SIEM platforms collect and correlate events from many systems.

course.learn: Centralized architecture concentrates control or services in one main location, while decentralized architecture distributes them across multiple nodes or locations.
course.why: Centralization simplifies governance but can create high-impact central dependencies; decentralization can improve resilience but complicate consistency and management.
course.example: A central identity service manages access for the enterprise, while a peer-to-peer ledger distributes validation across many participants.
course.exam: CompTIA may ask about single points of failure, management simplicity, resilience, and trust distribution.
